2024-06-15_155659.webp.description: Packing my bicycle for the flight.

2024-06-23_225338.webp.description: My belongings (many discarded later) laid out on the hotel bed.

2024-06-25_170800.webp.description: Dushanzi Grand Canyon viewed from WJ's drone.

2024-06-25_202553.webp.description: We were too excited and did not pace ourselves on the first day. Coupled with strong winds, we were so exhausted that we had to get off and push the bikes. You can see the Tianshan Mountains in the distance.

2024-06-26_094000.webp.description: Our tent pitched in the car park of a hotel under construction at Wusu tourism service area. None of us got up before 10am.

2024-06-26_222500.webp.description: Sheep at Maoliugou outpost, where we spent the second night. AP crashed on the descent and badly hurt his knee, so we hitched a lorry back to Kuitun Hospital the next day. He was back on the bike for a 1900m climb the day after (absolutely crazy).

2024-06-29_111000.webp.description: Starting the day with a 30km climb to Haxilegen Pass.

2024-06-29_114326.webp.description: A braided river spreading across the valley.

2024-06-29_160047.webp.description: The winding roads of Tianshan, and the steepest segment I have ever cycled to this day; the gradient never went below double digits (max gradient 39.6%).

2024-06-29_193800.webp.description: Snow at Haxilegen Pass, 3400m above sea level, the highest point of our trip and my first time at altitudes above 3000m. Every breath felt noticeably thinner.

2024-06-29_204500.webp.description: AP descending from Haxilegen Pass to Qiao'erma.

2024-06-29_213151.webp.description: A small stream near Qiao'erma. This scene looks straight out of a painting.

2024-07-01_132314.webp.description: Tangbula Grassland, where we did a chill recovery ride. None of us could take more climbs because no one was wearing cycling paddings (I thought they were unnecessary...).

2024-07-01_165401.webp.description: Our bikes parked at the roadside of Tangbula Grassland.

2024-07-01_182513.webp.description: WJ (left) and AP (right) looking at the distant peaks.

2024-07-02_155235.webp.description: Right before the tunnel of Yuximolegai Pass. We were soaked by the rain and had to wrap ourselves in emergency blankets. This was the closest I got to hypothermia.

2024-07-02_174500.webp.description: Heavy fog and rain after Yuximolegai Tunnel. Despite poor visibility, we had to descend to lower, warmer altitudes. I was seriously considering calling the emergency helpline, but we rolled a die and it told us not to (we survived).

2024-07-02_221330.webp.description: Sunset at Nalati Grassland after rain, fog, mud, and squeezing between heavy lorries in a big traffic jam.

2024-07-03_145800.webp.description: My bike covered in mud. A good 20km of the road to Nalati town was under construction and full of mud and potholes. We had to stay put that day to wash and dry essentially everything.
